entries.clue: Bill Gates' centre parting a puzzle (6)

indicatorNotes.centre: the centre of a word is its middle letter
indicatorNotes.parting: the letter splits the puzzle word in two, so it goes inside

annotation.surface: A remark about Bill Gates's hair, which is parted down the middle and apparently baffling.
annotation.walkthrough: Bill Gates reads as one name, but "Bill" is the definition and "Gates'" only donates its centre letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice stuck up in public, which is a poster.

entries.clue: Narrowly beat a seed (3)

blocks.note: British idiom: to win by a whisker, as at the post
the small seed of an apple or orange

annotation.surface: A tennis upset: an unseeded player just edges out a seed.
annotation.walkthrough: The sporting sense of "seed" is a decoy; here it is an apple pip.
annotation.definitionFit: To pip is to win narrowly, and a pip is also the seed of an apple or orange.

entries.clue: Press switches under network of veins keeping hairs rising (8,7)

indicatorNotes.switches: the letters of PRESS switch places
indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, the second part goes below the first
indicatorNotes.network of: a network is a tangle, so the letters of VEINS are rearranged
indicatorNotes.keeping: the rearranged VEINS holds CILIA inside it

annotation.surface: Something medical or cosmetic: pressing on a network of veins while hairs stand up.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word: "rising" as a noun, an uprising. Both anagrams are short, and CILIA sits inside the first.
annotation.definitionFit: The Sicilian Vespers was the 1282 rising in Sicily against French rule.

entries.clue: Up past one's bedtime in middle of schedule (6)

indicatorNotes.in: LATE goes inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.middle of: take the middle letters of the next word

blocks.note: the two middle letters of schEDule

annotation.surface: A child still up after bedtime, messing up the household schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: "Up" looks like part of "up past one's bedtime", but it stands alone as the definition: feeling up, cheerful.
annotation.definitionFit: Up, as in in high spirits, means elated.

entries.clue: Reckless plan to arrest a detective (6)

indicatorNotes.to arrest: to arrest is to hold, so MAP holds A DC

annotation.surface: A rash scheme to arrest a police detective.
annotation.walkthrough: "Arrest" fits the police picture, but here it only says MAP holds A DC.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a madcap scheme is one only a mad person would try, rash to the point of recklessness.

entries.clue: Trump's behind a force of the far right (3)

blocks.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

annotation.surface: A political jibe: behind Trump stands a force of the far right.
annotation.walkthrough: "Behind" reads as support, but "Trump's behind" is simply his backside, in American English an ass.
annotation.definitionFit: A behind is a backside, which Americans call an ass.

entries.clue: Game to truss and discard, stick around for Scottish pudding (7,8)

indicatorNotes.around: CLING wraps round the other pieces

blocks.note: loo is an old card game
to truss something is to tie it
to cling is to stick, split C...LING

annotation.surface: Instructions for game birds: truss them, throw out the rest, and hang around for dessert.
annotation.walkthrough: "Game" suggests birds to truss, but here it is LOO, the card game. A clootie dumpling is a spiced Scottish fruit pudding boiled in a cloth.
annotation.definitionFit: A clootie dumpling is a traditional Scottish pudding, named after the clout (cloth) it is boiled in.

entries.clue: Climbing near the summit, one's only risen a little (5)

indicatorNotes.Climbing: in a down clue, climbing reads upwards, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: at = near, as in at the door

annotation.surface: A mountaineer near the summit who has in fact climbed only a little way.
annotation.walkthrough: The climbing picture hides a bread: pitta is a flatbread, so it has risen only slightly.
annotation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat bread whose dough rises only a little.

entries.clue: Arrive as smoke (4,2)

blocks.note: a casual verb phrase for turning up, as guests do at a party
British slang for a cigarette made by hand from loose tobacco

annotation.surface: Someone turning up in a cloud of smoke.
annotation.walkthrough: A roll-up is British slang for a cigarette you roll yourself.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one phrase: the informal verb for turning up, and the noun for a hand-rolled cigarette.

entries.clue: Drink in remarkable actress, stop those playing to the crowds? (9,6)

indicatorNotes.remarkable: worth remarking on, out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A plea to a remarkable actress to have a drink and quit grandstanding.
annotation.walkthrough: "Playing to the crowds" sounds like a showy actress; the definition means games played in front of crowds.
annotation.definitionFit: Spectator sports are games played before crowds of watchers, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Work a deceit stopping one's business? (6)

blocks.note: go = work, as a machine goes

annotation.surface: A deceit at work that halts someone's company.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stopping" looks like an instruction to insert, but it belongs to the definition: a goalkeeper's business is stopping shots.
annotation.definitionFit: Stopping shots is a goalie's job, so stopping is a goalie's business.

entries.clue: Scent nothing gloomy (5)

annotation.surface: A scent that carries no gloom.
annotation.walkthrough: A plain charade.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name a smell, though odour often leans unpleasant where scent leans sweet.

entries.clue: Attempt to catch a partly abhorrent leader, failing (3,1,4)

indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.failing: failing, going wrong, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A plot to seize a leader who is, to some degree, abhorrent and now failing.
annotation.walkthrough: "Partly" looks like a hidden-word signal, but it is anagram fodder along with the A before it.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: setting a snare, literal or figurative, is an attempt to catch whoever walks into it.

entries.clue: All concluding philosophy so relaxing with a Hindu discipline (4)

indicatorNotes.All concluding: every word gives its concluding letter

blocks.note: last letters of philosophY sO relaxinG

annotation.surface: Praise for a relaxing Hindu philosophy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface describes the answer itself, which is part of the disguise.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by origin: the practice of postures and breathing began as one of the six orthodox schools of Hindu thought.

entries.clue: 20 with sweet cicely, 7 with an Israelite and 17 on the weekend, did you say - all in this? (5,6)

indicatorNotes.did you say: asks you to hear the pieces spoken aloud

blocks.note: sweet cicely is also called myrrh; 20 across is CURIE
17 down is EARN, after SAT, a weekend day
"this" is the place that holds all three planets just built

annotation.surface: A cryptic recipe or roll call with sweet cicely and an Israelite.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay makes three planets, not the answer: MERCURY, JUPITER and SATURN, each built from other answers and heard aloud. The definition is the place that holds them all.
annotation.definitionFit: Mercury, Jupiter and Saturn are all planets in the solar system.

entries.clue: A tangle to be taken down, erroneously pluralised slum resorts? (9)

annotation.definition: A tangle to be taken down

indicatorNotes.erroneously pluralised: GHETTO given a mock-Italian plural ending in I

blocks.note: a spa is a resort town
GHETTO wrongly pluralised the Italian way, O to I

annotation.surface: A mess of pulled-down resort slums, their name misspelt.
annotation.walkthrough: "Taken down" suggests demolition, but it means swallowed: spaghetti is a tangle you eat. "Ghetto" is Italian, so the joke plural is GHETTI.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: long strands of pasta end up in a knotted heap that you swallow, or take down.

entries.clue: Initially tie with red or white string (5)

indicatorNotes.Initially: initially means at the start, so only the word's opening letter is used

annotation.surface: Tying something with red or white string.
annotation.walkthrough: Red or white seem to be the string's colours; they are wines.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: strong string made of strands twisted together, the kind used to tie parcels.

entries.clue: Win to pick up having lost lead (4)

blocks.note: to pick up a language is to learn it

annotation.surface: A team trying to recover after losing the lead.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pick up" means learn, as in picking up a skill.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you win or gain wages, respect or a reward by deserving it.

entries.clue: Attempt to drink one litre, consuming bottle in frivolous manner (9)

indicatorNotes.to drink: to drink is to take something in, so TRY takes the next pieces inside it
indicatorNotes.consuming: consuming means eating up, so I L takes VIAL into its middle

blocks.note: a vial is a small bottle

annotation.surface: Someone trying to down a whole litre, bottle and all, just for fun.
annotation.walkthrough: The drinking picture points at the bottle as the drink, but the bottle is swallowed by the litre, and both by the attempt: two nested containers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: acting trivially means treating things as unimportant, which is frivolous.

entries.clue: Fruit settled on potato, dropping root (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, LIT sits on top of what follows
indicatorNotes.dropping root: in a down entry the root is the bottom, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a bird lit on a branch: settled

annotation.surface: A fruit fly settling on a potato that is losing its root.
annotation.walkthrough: A chip is a fried potato slice. "Root" is the bottom of a down entry, its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the lychee, spelt litchi in older books, is a sweet fruit with a rough red skin.

entries.clue: I preserve bottles in the name of pioneering scientific research (5)

annotation.definition: the name of pioneering scientific research

indicatorNotes.bottles: to bottle is to hold inside, so CURE holds I

blocks.note: to cure meat is to preserve it

annotation.surface: A scientist pickling specimens in the name of research.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bottles" and "preserve" fit the pickling lab, but bottles only puts I inside CURE.
annotation.definitionFit: Marie and Pierre Curie pioneered research into radioactivity.

entries.clue: Drunken search for another drink (6)

indicatorNotes.Drunken: drunk, reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

annotation.surface: A drunk hunting for one more drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The drunk picture is the whole disguise.
annotation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken after another, such as beer after a spirit.

entries.clue: See 27
Rings ending in trash, that was careless! (5)

indicatorNotes.ending in: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: oops is what you say after a slip

annotation.surface: Someone throwing rings at a bin, missing, and saying so.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation is the second piece, OOPS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hoop is a circular band, the ring thrown at a fairground stall.

entries.clue: Frog painter (6)

blocks.note: a whimsical noun for any creature that moves by jumping
Edward, the American realist behind Nighthawks

annotation.surface: A frog who paints.
annotation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings: an animal that hops, and Edward Hopper of Nighthawks.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a descriptive noun for a jumping animal, and the surname of the American painter Edward Hopper.

entries.clue: Holy man still holier as converted two-dimensional character (6,3,6)

indicatorNotes.as converted: converted, changed into something else, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Pope is a holy man

annotation.surface: A holy man growing holier still after a religious conversion.
annotation.walkthrough: "Converted" fits the religious picture but only rearranges HOLIER AS. A cartoon is two-dimensional.
annotation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor is a cartoon character, flat on the page or screen.

entries.clue: Female in the Wensleydale? (3)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is inside the next words

annotation.surface: A female found in Wensleydale.
annotation.walkthrough: Wensleydale is a Yorkshire valley known for its cheese and its sheep, so the ewe is really there.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the answer is the word for a female sheep, so "female" names it broadly.

entries.clue: Bum crack? (3,8)

blocks.note: the surface wants a backside; the setter means bum as an adjective, poor or worthless
the surface wants a cleft; the setter means a crack as a wisecrack, a joke

annotation.surface: A rude snigger at a bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: A crack is a joke and bum means bad, so a bum crack is a worn-out joke. The body reading is the trap.
annotation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a stale joke heard too often.

entries.clue: See 14
Primarily, frozen solid? (6)

annotation.surface: Something frozen solid.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: something frozen solid is frigid.
annotation.definitionFit: Frigid means intensely cold, as something frozen solid is.
